subject: Geography
examFormat: Three papers (1, 2 and 3), all compulsory; Papers 1 and 2 are a composite paper taken at one sitting. Paper 1: fifty objective questions, 1 hour, 50 marks, drawn from topics common to all member countries. Paper 2: nine essay questions, answer four, 2 hours, 80 marks; Nigerian candidates choose two questions from each of Section A (Economic and Human Geography) and Section B (Regional Geography of Nigeria). Paper 3 (Elements of Practical and Physical Geography): eight essay questions, answer four, 1 hour 50 minutes, 70 marks; Question 1 on map reading and interpretation is compulsory (25 marks), the others carry 15 marks each.
excluded: Topics marked * (Ghana, Sierra Leone, Liberia and The Gambia only): Principles of elementary surveying, Hydrosphere, Vegetation, Soil. Section B regional geography of Ghana, Sierra Leone, Liberia and Senegambia, and Section C Regional Geography of Africa (for non-Nigerian candidates only). Preamble, aims, scheme details and the suggested reading list.

subtopics.name: Maps: meaning, types and uses
objectives: Explain the meaning, types and uses of maps
Read and interpret contoured survey maps of parts of West Africa: scale, measurement of distances, direction and bearing, map reduction and enlargement
Identify physical features such as spurs, valleys etc. and cultural features such as city walls, settlements, communication routes etc.
Measure gradients, draw cross profiles and determine inter-visibility
Describe and explain drainage characteristics and pattern
Describe patterns of communication, settlement and land use

subtopics.name: Geographic Information System (GIS)
objectives: Explain the basic concepts of GIS
Identify its components: hardware, software, data, procedures and experts
Identify sources of data: land surveying, remote sensing, map digitizing, map scanning, field investigation, tabular data etc.
State uses of GIS: defence, agriculture, urban development, mapping, surveying, transportation, census etc.
Identify problems of GIS: power, personnel, capital etc.

subtopics.name: Statistical maps and diagrams
objectives: Represent statistical data graphically: bar graphs, line graphs, flow charts, dot maps, proportional circles, density maps, isopleth maps

topics.name: The earth as a planet
objectives: Describe the earth as a planet in relation to the sun
Explain latitude and distance, and longitude and time
Explain the earth's rotation and revolution and their effects
Describe the structure of the earth (internal and external)

topics.name: Rocks
objectives: Describe the types, characteristics, formation and uses of rocks

topics.name: Tectonic processes
objectives: Explain vulcanicity and earthquakes
Describe the formation, characteristics and importance of landforms: mountains, plains, karsts and coastal landforms

topics.name: Denudational processes
objectives: Describe agencies modifying landforms such as weathering, mass movement, running water, underground water, wind and waves

topics.name: Weather
objectives: Carry out simple weather study based on local observation
Describe the Stevenson's screen
Describe the uses of basic weather instruments, e.g. rain gauge, thermometer, barometer, wind vane

subtopics.name: Elements of climate
objectives: Describe rainfall, sunshine, air pressure, wind, humidity, temperature and cloud
Explain factors affecting climatic elements, e.g. altitude, latitude, ocean currents, land and sea breezes, continentality, aspect
Interpret climatic charts and data

subtopics.name: Classification of climate
objectives: Describe the major types of climate: hot climate (Equatorial, Tropical Continental, Desert) and temperate climate (warm and cool)
Describe the classification of climate based on Greek and Koppen

subtopics.name: Climate change
objectives: Explain the meaning, causes, effects and remedies of climate change

subtopics.name: Environmental resources
objectives: Explain the meaning of environmental resources
Classify them as renewable and non-renewable
Identify types (vegetation, water, mineral, atmospheric etc.) and state the importance of each

subtopics.name: Environmental problems and hazards
objectives: Identify types: soil erosion, drought, desert encroachment, flooding and pollution
State the causes, effects and prevention of each

subtopics.name: Environmental conservation
objectives: Explain the meaning, importance, methods, problems and solutions of environmental conservation

topics.name: World population
objectives: Explain the factors and patterns of growth, distribution and movement of population
Explain the problems of growth rate

topics.name: Settlement
objectives: Distinguish types of settlement (rural and urban)
Explain patterns and factors affecting location, growth and size
Describe the functions of rural and urban settlements
Describe interaction patterns: urban-rural, rural-urban, urban-urban, rural-rural
Explain migration

topics.name: Transportation
objectives: Describe the modes of transportation: roads, railways, water, air, pipeline, cables, ropeways etc.
Explain transportation and economic development: movement of people and commodities, national and international trade, diffusion of ideas and technology, national integration
Identify problems of transportation and their solutions

topics.name: Industry
objectives: Classify industries as primary, secondary and tertiary
Distinguish types of industry (heavy and light)
Explain factors of industrial location
State the contributions of industry to development
Identify problems of industry and their solutions

topics.name: Trade
objectives: Explain the meaning of trade
Distinguish types of trade (national and international)
State reasons for trade and its importance

topics.name: Tourism
objectives: Explain the meaning of tourism
Identify tourist centres and reasons for tourism (leisure, recreation, education etc.)
State the importance, problems and solutions of tourism

subtopics.name: Nigeria on broad outline
objectives: Describe the location, position, size, distance and political divisions of Nigeria

subtopics.name: Physical setting of Nigeria
objectives: Describe the relief, drainage, climate and vegetation of Nigeria

subtopics.name: Population of Nigeria
objectives: Describe the size, distribution, structure, population quality and population movement
Discuss population data: sources and problems/solutions

subtopics.name: Resources of Nigeria
objectives: Describe mineral resources (petroleum, gas, coal, tin/columbite, iron ore, limestone): distribution, methods of extraction, problems and solutions
Describe power resources (petroleum, gas, coal, HEP, solar energy)
Describe water resources (rivers, lakes, dams, sea, underground water)
Describe vegetation resources (trees, food and cash crops, timber etc.): forest, savanna, biosphere

subtopics.name: Agriculture in Nigeria
objectives: Describe types of agricultural practices, food and cash crops, importance, problems and solutions

subtopics.name: Transportation in Nigeria
objectives: Describe the modes of transportation, advantages and disadvantages, problems and solutions
Explain the influence of transportation on human activities

subtopics.name: Communication in Nigeria
objectives: Describe communication networks, advantages and disadvantages, importance, problems and solutions

subtopics.name: Industry in Nigeria
objectives: Define industry and describe its types and major industrial zones
Explain factors of location, importance, problems and solutions

subtopics.name: Trade in Nigeria
objectives: Explain the meaning and types (national and international) of trade
Describe the stock exchange, capital market, forex and major commercial areas
State the importance of commercial activities

subtopics.name: Tourism in Nigeria
objectives: Explain the meaning of tourism, tourist centres and reasons for tourism
State the importance, problems and solutions of tourism

subtopics.name: Issues on development and environmental concerns in Nigeria
objectives: Discuss issues of development and environmental conservation: rural and regional development, resource management and conservation
Discuss environmental pollution, e.g. air, water, soil, noise, and waste disposal

subtopics.name: ECOWAS
objectives: Explain the meaning of ECOWAS and list its member countries
State its purposes/mandate, advantages/benefits, disadvantages, problems and solutions

subtopics.name: Geo-political issues in Nigeria
objectives: Discuss geo-political issues: land reclamation

topics.name: Field work
objectives: Carry out fieldwork on any one of the following based on the local geography of the candidate's home country: land use (rural or urban), market survey (rural or urban), traffic flow (rural or urban), patterns of journey to work (rural or urban), or rate of erosion in the locality
topics.content: Land use: rural (crop farming e.g. rice, cocoa; urban crop farming; mining e.g. coal, tin, petroleum; fishing) or urban (commercial activities, ports, factories, recreation). This aspect of the syllabus is to be examined by schools as part of continuous assessment and accounts for 25% of the total mark allotted to continuous assessment.
